C++ API

While it is perfectly possible (and perhaps recommended) to interact with cuDART entirely through its Pythonic frontend, the user can also interface directly with the C++ executable through the command line. The C++ API can be found entirely within the src directory. Here we describe the functionality of the main classes used within cuDART.

  1. The vec3 class

  2. The Ray class

  3. The Camera class

  4. The MeshBlock class

  5. The Mesh class

Outside of this class structure, the main code routines can be split into

  1. Kernels

  2. Tools

Included within the C++ API is npy.hpp, which provides functionality for reading and writing .npy files with C++. This library is imported verbatim from the libnpy repository created by Leon Merten Lohse (github) under MIT license. We do not include documentation for this librarhy here, please refer to the original libnpy repository.

For brevity, this page gives only simple descriptions of classes, member and non-member functions. For a full description of class attributes and function parameters, refer to the source code within the src directory. Life is too short to use Doxygen, Breathe, Sphinx and ReadTheDocs to auto-document relatively straightforward C++ code…

Classes

class vec3

The vec3 class is used to support basic vector arithmetic in C++, such as normalisation, dot and cross products and rotations about another vector.

class Ray

The Ray class describes a line-of-sight for a pixel, defined by an origin and a normal vector

vec3 march(float s)

Return the point given by traversing a distance s from the origin along the normal vector

class Camera

The Camera class is responsible for loading in camera properties and genrating rays for each pixels in an image

void build_camera()

Generates an image plane using internal positional and orientional arguments

vec3 calc_pixel_origin(const int i, const int j)

Returns the ray origin for a pixel given its 2D indices in the image plane

class MeshBlock

The MeshBlock class is the keystone of the C++ API, responsible for containing a regular simulation sub-domain and providing methods to calculate line-of-sight summations over this sub-domain using the DDA alogorithm.

bool calc_mb_intercept(const Ray *r, float &s_entry, float &s_exit)

Determine if intersection occurs between a Ray and the MeshBlock; if so then store the entry and exit locations as parameterised by s_entry and s_exit

float calc_trace(const Ray &r, TraceArgs trace_args)

Calculate a summation through the MeshBlock sub-domain, on a path given by a Ray’s line of sight. Apply runtime flags stored within the TraceArgs struct.

class Mesh

Akin to the Pythonic Mesh class, in the C++ code the Mesh class is a container for all sub-domains, labelling MeshBlocks within a single snapshot of the simulation. The Mesh able to accept lines-of-sight generated within the Camera class and iterate over all MeshBlocks to perform the path summation. Unlike the Pythonic Mesh, in C++ Mesh is used regardless of running in labelled or unlabelled mode.

float calc_trace(const Ray &r, TraceArgs trace_args)

Calculate the total summation through the full domain for a given ray’s line-of-sight, summing over contributions from each MeshBlock

Kernels

Kernels are functions called from the host, but deployed on the device. All kernels have __global__ scope.

render_from_mesh(Camera camera, float *img, Mesh **mesh, TraceArgs trace_args)

Principle render kernel, calculates pixel values on a thread-by-thread basis

init_mesh(Mesh **mesh, MeshBlock **mb_list, int num_meshblocks)

Allocated and initialises a Mesh container on the device

free_mesh(Mesh **mesh, int num_meshblocks)

Deletes Mesh container from device, frees each MeshBlock

init_meshblock(MeshBlockInfo mb_info, MeshBlock **mb_list, float *data)

Builds MeshBlock on device, adds to list

wipe_img(Camera camera, float *img)

Sets all values in the image buffer to zero as prep for next render
